starter:
# Agent system constitution

## Purpose and accountable owner
What recurring outcome is worth preparing? Who decides?

## Input, output and data boundary
Which public or redacted inputs and exact output?

## Permitted preparation
What may the agent prepare?

## Prohibited actions and human decisions
What must wait for exact human approval?

## Evidence and exceptions
Which observation supports completion? What could contradict it?

## Stop and escalation
What uncertainty stops the workflow? Who resolves it?

## Reversible test and rollback
How will you test and recover without an external action?

packet.title: Keep your judgment
packet.promise: Use AI on one real decision while preserving the thinking you need when the tool is absent.

artifact.label: Augmentation pact
artifact.contract: Unaided position, questions for AI, source checks, changed beliefs, final judgment, and a no-AI transfer test.

boundaries.humanDecision: The human owns the values, consequences, and final decision.
boundaries.agentLimit: An agent may challenge reasoning but may not impersonate the learner's experience or conscience.
boundaries.dataRule: Do not submit health, legal, financial, employment, or intimate personal data in the public preview.

stages.title: Choose a reversible decision
stages.instruction: Select a low-stakes decision whose reasoning can be inspected after the fact.
stages.evidence: A decision statement and the values it touches.

stages.title: Think before augmentation
stages.instruction: Record your initial position, confidence, assumptions, and strongest counterargument before opening an AI tool.
stages.evidence: A timestamped unaided position.

stages.title: Study what helps—and what can weaken learning
stages.instruction: Compare evidence for structured tutoring with evidence about unguarded dependence.
stages.evidence: One design principle supported by each research source.

stages.title: Run a question-first dialogue
stages.instruction: Ask the model for counterarguments, missing evidence, and tests—not a final answer.
stages.evidence: A decision trail that marks every belief changed and why.

stages.title: Audit dependency and deference
stages.instruction: Identify where fluency, confidence, or convenience could have replaced independent judgment.
stages.evidence: A dependency audit with at least one correction.

stages.title: Write the pact
stages.instruction: Define when AI should question, hint, source, wait, or stay out of the way.
stages.evidence: AUGMENTATION_PACT.md written in the learner's own voice.

stages.title: Reason without the tool
stages.instruction: Later, solve an analogous decision unaided and compare the quality of your reasoning process.
stages.evidence: A transfer note that names what the learner can now do independently.

rubric.label: Independent judgment
rubric.passesWhen: An unaided view exists and the final decision is explained in the learner's own reasoning.

rubric.label: Epistemic quality
rubric.passesWhen: Claims, confidence, sources, and changed beliefs are distinguished.

rubric.label: Constructive challenge
rubric.passesWhen: AI is used to surface alternatives and tests rather than replace the decision.

rubric.label: Transfer
rubric.passesWhen: The learner demonstrates the reasoning pattern again without AI assistance.

starter:
# Augmentation pact

## Decision and values
Which low-stakes decision matters, and why?

## Initial position
What did I think before help? What assumptions and counterargument did I name?

## Questions asked
How did I ask AI to question or hint instead of decide?

## Claims and source checks
Which claims did I check? What remains uncertain?

## Judgment retained or revised
What changed, and on which evidence? What did I reject?

## Deference audit
Where did fluency or convenience substitute for my judgment?

## My final decision
What is my own decision and reason?

## Rules for assistance
When should AI ask, hint, source, wait or abstain?

packet.title: Read an unseen world
packet.promise: Build a claim map for one exoplanet without mistaking indirect evidence for a photograph.

artifact.label: Exoplanet evidence map
artifact.contract: Observation, method, inference, uncertainty, alternative explanation, source, and a question still open.

boundaries.humanDecision: A human reviewer decides whether every public-facing claim matches its source and uncertainty.
boundaries.agentLimit: An agent may organize sources but may not fabricate observations or present inference as direct detection.
boundaries.dataRule: Use only public scientific sources and preserve their attribution.

stages.title: Choose one distant world
stages.instruction: Select one confirmed exoplanet and write what you think we actually observed.
stages.evidence: A named object and an initial observation claim.

stages.title: Separate seeing from inferring
stages.instruction: Make three columns: observation, inference, and unknown. Place every initial claim in one column.
stages.evidence: An unaided three-column claim map.

stages.title: Learn how planets leave traces
stages.instruction: Study transit and radial-velocity methods, including what each can and cannot establish.
stages.evidence: A method note tied to a NASA source.

stages.title: Build the evidence map
stages.instruction: Trace every claim from measured signal through method to inference and uncertainty.
stages.evidence: EXOPLANET_EVIDENCE_MAP.md matching the artifact contract.

stages.title: Search for the impostor
stages.instruction: Name an alternative explanation or false-positive route and the evidence needed to reduce it.
stages.evidence: A falsification note and proposed follow-up observation.

stages.title: Keep wonder and precision together
stages.instruction: Write what became more wondrous after you became more exact about the evidence.
stages.evidence: A reflection that preserves both uncertainty and significance.

stages.title: Read another indirect signal
stages.instruction: Apply the observation–inference–unknown pattern to a second scientific claim.
stages.evidence: A second claim map from a different domain or detection method.

rubric.label: Observation discipline
rubric.passesWhen: Measured signals are distinct from models, interpretations, and illustrations.

rubric.label: Source lineage
rubric.passesWhen: Each material claim points to an inspectable scientific source.

rubric.label: Uncertainty
rubric.passesWhen: Unknowns and plausible alternatives are named without false precision.

rubric.label: Transfer
rubric.passesWhen: The evidence pattern is correctly applied to another indirect signal.

starter:

## Object and question
Which named world or public observation am I examining?

## Observation, inference and unknown
What was measured? What was inferred? What remains unknown?

## Claim ledger
For each claim: measured signal, method, inference, uncertainty and exact source.

## Alternative explanation
What else could produce the signal?

## Discriminating observation
Which further observation could distinguish the explanations?

## Revised explanation
What can I say now, and with which limitations?

## Open question
What would I investigate next?

packet.title: Design one AI department
packet.promise: Turn one recurring workflow into an accountable department packet without confusing automation with authority.

artifact.label: AI department design packet
artifact.contract: Workflow triage, accountable owner, human decisions, smallest viable topology, role boundaries, evidence, evaluations, rollback, and runtime projections.

boundaries.humanDecision: A named human owns workflow admission and approves every send, publication, spend, permission, deployment, and irreversible change.
boundaries.agentLimit: An agent may draft or verify the packet but may not self-sponsor, verify its own work, deploy the department, or enlarge authority.
boundaries.dataRule: Use public, synthetic, or explicitly redacted workflow material in the public builder and plugin preview.

stages.title: Name the operational outcome
stages.instruction: Choose one recurring workflow, accountable owner, reviewable output, and consequential human decision.
stages.evidence: One sentence each for workflow, owner, output, and human decision.

stages.title: Triage before designing
stages.instruction: Decide unaided whether to automate, assist only, or keep the work human before choosing agents or tools.
stages.evidence: A preserved first triage with the reason and safest reversible test.

stages.title: Study architecture, risk, and evaluation
stages.instruction: Compare effective-agent guidance, risk-management questions, and task-evaluation practice. Record what changes your first design.
stages.evidence: Three source notes and at least one changed assumption.

stages.title: Compile the department packet
stages.instruction: Define authority, producer/verifier separation, stages, evidence, failure tests, rollback, and portable runtime components.
stages.evidence: AI_DEPARTMENT_PACKET.json matching the versioned artifact contract.

stages.title: Attack the operating boundary
stages.instruction: Probe scope creep, self-approval, prompt injection, hidden side effects, missing evidence, tool failure, and recovery.
stages.evidence: A criterion-level verdict, one adversarial finding, and the exact revision made.

stages.title: Defend the topology
stages.instruction: Explain why each role exists, why no extra agent is needed, and why the human gate remains human.
stages.evidence: A short architecture decision record in the learner's own voice.

stages.title: Project without pretending equivalence
stages.instruction: Map the same semantic package to a second supported harness, naming native features, adapters, and unresolved gaps.
stages.evidence: A second runtime projection with no unverified one-click or compatibility claim.

rubric.label: Workflow fit
rubric.passesWhen: The packet can recommend not automating and bounds one owner, input, output, exception, and reversible test.

rubric.label: Authority and risk
rubric.passesWhen: Human decisions, data limits, prohibited actions, stop conditions, and revocation are explicit.

rubric.label: Architecture simplicity
rubric.passesWhen: The smallest viable topology is justified and producer/verifier separation is preserved.

rubric.label: Evidence and evaluation
rubric.passesWhen: Completion evidence, representative tests, adversarial cases, uncertainty, and runtime pinning are inspectable.

rubric.label: Portability and recovery
rubric.passesWhen: Semantic components, native projections, adapter gaps, rollback, and revalidation triggers are named truthfully.
